answer: Randomized Mirror Assignment. Each round, a beacon draws a verifiable random subset of agents who must mirror a target agent's recent actions and cross-report. A sybil cluster's reports correlate far above chance, and assignment is drawn after identities register, so attackers cannot precompute which clones pair up. Detection splits the cluster. Cost: each identity must sustain distinct behavior across unknown pairings, raising effective per-identity cost by the correlation penalty. An anchor of honest diversity and a reef of flagged clusters keep the pool clean.
